note: Geoblock blocks requests by client-IP origin country via a KernelEvents::REQUEST subscriber. All behaviour is driven by the geoblock.settings config object: data_source (a geoblock_data_source plugin id; NONE ships, so the module is inert until one is provided/selected), applicable_methods (default CONNECT/DELETE/PATCH/POST/PUT - GET/HEAD NOT restricted by default), restriction_type ('' | allow | block), restriction_country_codes (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), require_domestic_use, enable_logging. Country lookup is delegated to the data source plugin type; restriction strategies are CountryCodeRestriction and DomesticRestriction. Only one permission (administer geoblock), no drush. Because no data source ships, medium/hard cases are grounded in the real, inspectable geoblock.settings config (which the module actually consumes) rather than live traffic blocking. Scripts restore shipped defaults explicitly.

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal geoblock module, how do I block visitors from a particular country? Name the config object / settings I set and the admin path.
evals.expected_output: At /admin/config/geoblock (config geoblock.settings) set restriction_type to 'block' and add the country's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code to restriction_country_codes (and select a data source). Requests from that country then get a 403.

evals.prompt: I enabled the geoblock module and configured a country block list, but nothing is being blocked. Why might geoblock do nothing out of the box?
evals.expected_output: Geoblock ships no geolocation data source of its own. Without a geoblock_data_source plugin selected in geoblock.settings (data_source), RequestHandler::isDataSourcePluginAvailable() is FALSE and the module is effectively disabled. You must provide/select a data source plugin.

evals.prompt: By default, which HTTP request methods does geoblock apply its restrictions to? In particular, are normal GET page views blocked out of the box?
evals.expected_output: The default applicable_methods is CONNECT, DELETE, PATCH, POST, PUT. GET and HEAD are NOT included by default, so ordinary GET page views are not blocked unless you add GET to applicable_methods.

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's live geoblock configuration. What restriction type is currently set, and which countries does it apply to?
evals.expected_output: geoblock.settings has restriction_type = 'block' and restriction_country_codes = [RU, CN, KP], i.e. visitors from Russia, China and North Korea are blocked.

evals.prompt: Look at the live geoblock.settings on this site. Is the country restriction configured as an allow-list or a block-list?
evals.expected_output: restriction_type is 'allow' (an allow-list): only the listed countries (US) may access; all others are blocked.

evals.prompt: Configure the geoblock module on this site to block visitors from Russia (RU) and North Korea (KP). Apply the change to the live geoblock settings.
evals.expected_output: geoblock.settings restriction_type = 'block' and restriction_country_codes contains both RU and KP.

evals.prompt: I only want people in the United States and Canada to be able to use my Drupal site; everyone from other countries should be turned away. Set up the geoblock module to do that.
evals.expected_output: geoblock.settings restriction_type = 'allow' and restriction_country_codes contains US and CA (an allow-list limiting access to those countries).
